messages:
Maria: Quick question — we need to lock down the routing policy schema for customer tiers + regional fallback. The PR currently applies quota checks after routing which can cause weird billing spikes if a higher-tier model is selected then the quota is enforced. Thoughts?
Kevin: Can you show the minimal repro? I think ordering matters: quota check -> route selection vs route selection -> quota check.
Maria: Repro snippet (simplified):
```yaml
routing: 
  tiers:
    free:
      max_tokens_per_month: 1_000_000  # soft
      hard_limit: true
      preferred_variants: [gpt-small, gpt-small-quant]  
    pro:
      max_tokens_per_month: 50_000_000
      hard_limit: false
      preferred_variants: [gpt-medium, gpt-medium-quant]
  region_fallback: [us-west, eu-west, ap-sg]
```
If we pick route first (chooses gpt-medium in us-west) then check quota, the free tenant gets error after the tokens are consumed.
Sasha: IMO: soft quotas should be enforced via policy that allows automatic fallback to cheaper variant. Hard quotas should abort before routing. So enforcement stage depends on quota type. :thumbsup:
Tiago: That matches my read. Two execution hooks: pre-route (hard limits) and post-route (soft-budget enforcement that triggers fallback to `cheaper_variant`).
Ben: UX note — Console should show a per-tenant "fallbacks triggered" counter and a timeline of when quota-caused fallbacks happened. Otherwise SRE gets paged and we have no context.
Maria: Agree. Also telemetry event names: `quota.check` (result: hard_block|soft_fallback|ok) and `route.selection` with chosen_variant and reason. We need atomic correlation id so console can join them.
Kevin: Implementation question: do we encode this in the policy DSL or keep it as separate enforcement engine? My preference: keep routing decisions pure (cost/latency/region) and let enforcement layer mutate the decision only for soft quotas. That way routing telemetry stays consistent.
Sasha: Counterpoint: if enforcement mutates decisions, telemetry will show pre/post diffs which is helpful to see why a decision changed. But we need both pre and post events.
policy-bot: New spec proposal posted: https://go/repo/PR/1234 (draft) — includes pre/post hooks and new quota semantics.
Tiago: One edge case: what if region fallback picks a cheaper region with same variant but different latency — do we allow enforcement to change region? That can surprise customers. I think enforcement can only change variant, not region, unless customer config allows region fallback on budget.
Maria: Good call. Add `allow_enforcement_region_change: bool` flag per-tenant, default false.
Ben: Also add a dashboard filter for "enforcement-origin" = [policy|client|system] so we can spot misconfigs.
Kevin: For API, propose semantics: POST /v1/route -> returns {route_plan, enforcement_actions: [soft_fallback->variant], final_route}. Clients can opt-in to see pre-enforcement plan with `?explain=true`.
Sasha: Please make sure `explain=true` respects PII/data policies; only metadata.
Maria: Action items: Kevin to update PR with two-stage enforcement (pre-route hard checks, post-route soft fallbacks) + telemetry events. Sasha to add console widgets for fallback timeline. Tiago to add policy flag for region-change opt-in. Ben to draft dashboard filters. I'll follow up in PR comments. :white_check_mark:
Kevin: Assigning to me, will aim for EOD tomorrow.
Maria: Thanks — if anyone has edge cases, drop them here.
Ben: Edge case: multi-variant pipelines (reranker + generator) — enforcement needs to consider combined token budget, not just generator. Will open an issue.
policy-bot: Reminder: RFC review tomorrow 10:30 PT in #eng-platform.
